observation.visible_scene: A sunset over a calm sea. A bright orange-yellow sun disk sits directly on the flat horizon line, casting a vertical, broken column of shimmering reflection down the water toward the foreground. The sky grades from deep orange at the horizon to a muted gray-brown overhead. A faint low landmass silhouette is visible on the left horizon and a thin dark breakwater/structure on the right. The lower portion of the frame is a wet, gently rippled beach/shallow water showing a separate small orange reflection patch. The overall composition (horizon height, sun position) stays fixed across the excerpt.
visible_changes: The sea surface shows continuous small ripples/wavelets; their crests shift slightly frame to frame.
The sun's vertical reflection column flickers and changes shape/brightness segment by segment as the water moves beneath it; this is modulation of the reflection, not movement of the sun.
The lower foreground reflection patch likewise shifts and re-forms with the wet-sand ripples.
The sun disk and the horizon remain essentially stationary relative to the frame; no clear sinking or rising is measurable within this short excerpt.
Occasional tiny dark specks appear briefly in the upper sky area (e.g. near the top edge in some frames), not consistently present.
Sky brightness/contrast varies subtly between frames, consistent with slow exposure/lighting drift rather than a discrete event.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the sun continues to set below the horizon after this segment, and how the sky color evolves later.
Any earlier state of the water or sun before t=0.
The true cause of the brief specks (birds, insects, or sensor dust) and whether they belong to the scene.
uncertain_details: Camera motion: the horizon and sun hold nearly constant positions, so the camera appears static, but a very slight drift cannot be ruled out from background evidence alone.
Whether the sun dips a few pixels over the 3.3 s is not clearly discernible; treat its vertical position as effectively unchanged.
The lower orange blob is interpreted as a reflection on wet sand/shallow water, not a separate illuminated object.
